lines.text: Being cruel to an AI, just for fun, is about to break the rules.
On October 8, Anthropic updated the usage policy for its Claude chatbot. It takes effect November 12.
The new rule bars "sustained and needless abusive or cruel behavior" toward its AI models.
Venting is still fine. So are pushback, dark creative writing, and testing or research.
The main penalty? Claude ends the conversation. That chat is closed, but you can start a new one.
Claude has been able to end persistently abusive chats since August 2025.
The rule covers every Claude user, even on the free plan. Anthropic hasn't said whether accounts can be banned.
Why it matters: AI companies are now writing rules about how we treat the AI itself.
